post.caption: Some kanzashi had a tiny earpick. Kanzashi began as plain working hairpins for holding hair. An old belief said a pointed stick could ward off evil. In the Edo period, hair ornaments reflected age and social class. Some had dangling ornaments that swayed as the wearer walked. Ball tipped ones were topped with coral or agate. Silk flower kanzashi are pinched from tiny squares with tweezers. That craft is called tsumami, which means pinching. Each finished flower dries for about 24 hours. Kyoto apprentice geisha wear a new flower ornament each month. Cherry blossom is for April and willow is for June.
